_comment: Floors gate on testable coverage: the denominator excludes the UI and lifecycle files listed in scripts/coverage-exclude.json. The run-to-run allowance is APP_FLOOR_TOLERANCE (1.5 points) in scripts/enforce_coverage_floors.py, so a new or re-baselined floor is the measured value rounded down to 4 places. The floors set on 2026-09-02 were recorded at least 2 points below the measured value and keep that margin until they are next re-baselined. `overall` and `modules` block the required check only when coverage is more than that tolerance below the floor. When code moves between files, re-measure every row it touches from one complete CI run: #1603 moved the network-loss handler out of MyBooksDownloadCenter, so that row was re-baselined to 0.6405 and DownloadNetworkLossMonitor was added at its measured 1.0 (#1601). Raise floors as unit-testable coverage grows, not by adding paths to the exclude list. A module in `modules` with no coverage data fails the gate; record a deliberate exemption in `unmeasured` with the reason instead.
_comment_packages: `packages`, `host_packages` and `package_modules` are advisory: a row below its floor prints `FAIL advisory` and does not change the exit code, because these measurements varied by up to 1.2 points between CI runs of identical code (#1601). A floor in these scopes with no data still fails. Values are the lower of two measurements (unit-testing runs 37333831409 and 37350306572, 2026-10-05), rounded down to 4 places. `packages` is package source measured by the app suite on the iOS simulator; `host_packages` is the same source measured by the package's own `swift test` on macOS; the two use different instrumentation and are never combined. `package_modules` holds floors for modules whose source moved into a package (TPPBookRegistry, now in PalaceBookRegistry). All three are compared only when the run collected package source (CI does; a local Xcode run does not).
